description: rg -rn is never a valid flag combo: rg parses -r <text> as REPLACE-with-literal. Run 01M22X87J1RKQ6A8FZB7RC2RN8: 'rg -rn "is_engine_stamped_key"' replaced every match with literal 'n', producing 'pub fn n(key: &str...)', which was then misdiagnosed as 'sandbox rg unreliable' (false lore, cost 2 diagnostic rounds). Use -n alone for line numbers.
resolution: Discipline line added to .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/implementer.md retracting the 'sandbox rg unreliable' lore (seed fabro-2eb6).

description: Changing the embedded FABRO_GIT_SHA length (fabro_build_support::SHORT_SHA_LEN, fabro-6ffb 7->12) silently breaks the fabro-test insta BUILD filter regex (lib/foundation/fabro-test/src/lib.rs INSTA_FILTERS, the ([0-9a-f]{7} date...) pattern) because the filter hardcodes the old length: version snapshots then diff on every commit. Length-bearing snapshot filters must be updated in the same diff as the length constant; symptom is a snapshot diff showing a raw sha where [BUILD] used to be.
resolution: Updated the filter to {12} in the same diff (fabro-6ffb); future length changes must grep INSTA_FILTERS for the old length before landing.

description: Piping  into a python one-liner that crashes still creates the record — the CLI already wrote it (fabro sprint 19: d7e7+3523 silently duplicated f93b+c167 and had to be closed as dupes). Same class as the fabro create ghost-run rule.

description: Semantics change in fabro-tool inherit_parent_target (fabro-b4ed, run 01M2GVW7GGGB19ZZ9NBN2H5FDC) passed the implementer's crate-scoped verify but red-lined the tester: the fabro-server integration fixture lib/apps/fabro-server/src/run_tool_create.rs builds a parent via test_run_spec() whose pull_request settings stay None, so under the new option-(a) semantics the child correctly inherits the base branch and the checkout assertion reads 'original'. Lesson: any change to inherited-target semantics must update downstream fixture parents to enable pull_request settings when the test means to exercise run-branch chaining. Also: after editing a src-integrated test file, confirm nextest actually recompiled — a stale binary reported the pre-edit panic line.
resolution: Fixture parent now sets pull_request enabled before inherit, matching the new chaining precondition; test passes and full fabro-server suite is green (939/939).

description: A tracker close reason containing BACKTICKS was passed through the bash() command line (seeds close <id> --reason "..."): bash executed the backticked fragments as command substitution. 'start -> env_guard -> tracker_guard' ran the command 'start' with stdout REDIRECTED to env_guard and tracker_guard, which CREATED three empty files at the repo root; the recorded close reason lost every backticked phrase. It went unnoticed until but status showed three 'A' entries beside the tracker file.
resolution: For any CLI write whose text may contain backticks, $() or >, write the payload to a file and pass it as --reason "$(cat /tmp/reason.txt)" (command substitution happens once, on that path only). After every shell-based tracker write, run but status / git status and remove stray A entries before committing — a stray file would otherwise ride the next sweep commit.

description: rg -rn does NOT mean recursive+line-numbers in the way expected: -r takes the NEXT TOKEN as its REPLACE value, so -rn silently replaces every match with the literal n in the OUTPUT (observed twice in one session 2026-10-14: EnvironmentErrorKind::n in results, gate-measure scan confusion). Use -n -r separately or omit -r; the corrupted display looks like real source content.
resolution: Never write -rn; use rg -n alone, and -r VALUE as an explicit separate flag.

content: The fabro-test workbench has a SINGLE-PROBE mode: `nu scripts/workbench.nu probe <name>` (plus --expect to override) — it runs one facet without board clean, platform checks, or the mini integration. During incident triage, NEVER re-run the full bench to re-check one facet: identify the suspected rows first (run list via `fabro ps -a --json` + bench label, or the platform checks via `source scripts/workbench.nu; platform-checks`), then re-run exactly those. User directive 2026-10-27 after three full bench runs (~15 min and real model cost each) where a single probe would have answered.

GitHub read-after-write races: any immediate read that follows a create (label-filtered list, PR body fetch, issue read) races the index and must poll (~2s convergence, 6x2s is the proven pattern). Two witnesses now: the P4 work-CLI list row (sprint 53, denkhaus/work#10..#12) and the publish-bridge PR body fetch (bench 1027-162117: PR #87 body was generated prose but the immediate fetch failed the bridge; fixed in fabro-test PR #88 with the same poll).

description: Literal parentheses inside a nu $"..." interpolation are parsed as a subexpression and executed as a command — scripts/verify.nu:292 prints a status line containing '(full crate suite: ...)' inside $"" and crashes with 'Command full not found' exactly when the full-crate-suite test arm fires (any implementer diff that edits existing tests in a touched crate).
resolution: Workaround in run 01M621RW4YPD19X5E2VMC054YW: run the intended nextest slice directly (cargo nextest run -p <crate> --no-fail-fast). Durable fix is a loop-asset item: strip the literal parens or build the label by concatenation.

name: gate-red triage: parent-commit worktree repro with shared target dir
description: When a tester gate-red bounces the implementer, classify item-caused vs pre-existing environmental by reproducing ONE representative failing test on the untouched parent commit in a throwaway worktree sharing the main target dir: git worktree add /tmp/qg-parent <parent-sha> && CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<repo>/target cargo nextest run -p <crate> <test>. Build cost ~2-5 min once; a reproduce-on-parent FAIL proves the break is environmental/pre-existing (this run: docker daemon absent + engine-injected FABRO_SERVER default breaking parse_settings_command and all docker-acquiring CLI it-tests, fabro run 01M621RW4YPD19X5E2VMC054YW), which routes Blocked instead of chasing phantom regressions in the item diff.

Literal parentheses inside a nu $"..." interpolation are parsed as a subexpression and executed as a command — scripts/verify.nu:292 prints a status line containing '(full crate suite: ...)' inside $" interpolation, so every verify run that reaches the full-crate-suite arm dies with 'Command full not found' before running nextest. RECURRED run 01M621RW4YPD19X5E2VMC054YW (implementer visit 2, again blocking the fabro-cli full-suite arm). Still unfixed in scripts/verify.nu.
resolution: Open loop-asset bug (scripts/verify.nu is fs_hide-bound for the implementer; report-don't-fix). Interim workaround: when the verify run dies at line 292, run the intended 'cargo nextest run -p <crate> --no-fail-fast' directly. Durable fix belongs to a loop-asset item: strip the parens or build the label by string concatenation.

content: just vendor <cmd> --message breaks on any multi-word message: the recipe passes *args into `nu scripts/vendor-sync.nu {{ args }}` UNQUOTED - bash chokes on parens, nu sees extra positionals. Call `nu scripts/vendor-sync.nu export petri --message "..."` directly (same ceremony, quoting survives, multiline bodies work). AGENTS.md documents the just form only.
The repo grep TOOL silently finds nothing under vendor/petri (ignore-file handling); ripgrep via shell with --no-ignore sees the tree. Any vendor-tree search: rg --no-ignore.
